solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fellow's beginning to influence Gallery? Demur

parts.note: fellow gives HE, and the 's stands for 'is', making HE'S

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only the opening letter of influence is used

parts.note: the Tate is the famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a man's start might sway an art gallery, then voices an objection.
explanation.walkthrough: TATE is London's best-known gallery (several branches, including Tate Modern).
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to hold back or hesitate over going along with something; a synonym pair.

clue.text: He entertains large number

definitions.meaning: someone who entertains guests at home or at a party
a great crowd or multitude, as in a heavenly throng

explanation.surface: A man who keeps a great many people amused.
explanation.definitionFit: A host receives guests, and a host is also a multitude, as in 'a host of problems'.

clue.text: Move fast chasing second allocation

indicators.note: chasing means coming after, so the speed word follows the abbreviation

parts.note: to hare is to run very fast

explanation.surface: Someone rushes after their second helping or portion.
explanation.definitionFit: A share is a portion allotted to someone, the same as an allocation.

clue.text: Bitterness about shout of triumph in shelter? Cowboy wears it

indicators.note: in places the three pieces before it inside the shelter word

parts.note: a tent is a simple shelter
gall means bitterness or resentment
on means about or concerning
HA is an exclamation of triumph

explanation.surface: Bitter about a cheer inside shelter, with a cowboy's headgear in view.
explanation.definitionFit: The ten-gallon hat is the large, high-crowned hat associated with cowboys of the American West.

clue.text: Named songbird was first

parts.note: the tit is a small songbird
to have led is to have been first or in front

explanation.surface: A particular songbird got its name before others.
explanation.definitionFit: Titled means given a title or name, so it can stand for named.

clue.text: Act the same on return

indicators.note: the word reads identically when it is run backwards, so turning it round changes nothing

parts.note: an act; the setter has the word serve as both definition and the thing read backwards

explanation.surface: A performance that is identical when repeated on the way back.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is just the observation that the four-letter answer is a palindrome.
explanation.definitionFit: A deed is an action or act, as in 'a good deed'; a straight synonym.

clue.text: Dictator in river — investigate

indicators.note: in puts the dictator inside the river name

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, England
Idi Amin was the dictator of Uganda

explanation.surface: A tyrant is found in the water and someone looks into it.
explanation.walkthrough: The Exe is a river in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine is to inspect closely, a synonym for investigate.

clue.text: Take income from detective post? That hurts

parts.note: DI is Detective Inspector
to post is to send
OW is the cry when something hurts

explanation.surface: A police officer complains as their post pays no more.
explanation.definitionFit: To disendow is to strip an institution, typically a church, of its endowment funds.

clue.text: An inane nark, annoying at first, transformed into classic work

indicators.note: transformed means changed in form, so the letters are rearranged into something new
at first means only the opening letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A silly informer, irritating to begin with, becomes a great book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transformed into' rearranges ANINANENARK to ANNAKARENIN; 'at first' adds the A from annoying at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Anna Karenina is Tolstoy's celebrated novel, a classic of world literature.

clue.text: Error about Washington lover

indicators.note: the error word goes round the outside of the state abbreviation, sitting about it

parts.note: a sin is a wrongdoing or error
WA is the abbreviation for Washington State

explanation.surface: A mistake made concerning a lover in Washington.
explanation.definitionFit: A swain is an old poetic term for a young male suitor or sweetheart.

clue.text: Pacific islanders not about to meet difficulty on way back

indicators.note: about here means turned about, so the word not is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written before being turned round

indicators.note: on the way back means travelling in reverse, so the word for difficulty is read backwards

parts.note: a snag is a difficulty or hitch

explanation.surface: Islanders from the Pacific avoid running into trouble on their homeward journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses NOT to TON; 'on way back' reverses SNAG to GANS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongans are the people of Tonga, an island kingdom in the South Pacific.

clue.text: Shockingly axe grannie, as senior citizen

indicators.note: something done shockingly is done in a wild, disordered way, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A grim headline: someone shockingly attacks a grandmother, an elderly person.
explanation.definitionFit: A person in their sixties is a sexagenarian, typically counted as an older or senior citizen.

clue.text: He does odd jobs, hard, with many shifts

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
and means with, joined to

indicators.note: shifts means moves around, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A worker on lots of tough shifts takes on odd tasks.
explanation.definitionFit: A handyman is someone employed to do various small repairs and odd jobs.

clue.text: Answer very frivolously or with enthusiasm?

parts.note: idly means in a frivolous, purposeless way

explanation.surface: Should one reply lightly or with real keenness?
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something avidly means doing it eagerly and keenly, the same as with enthusiasm.

clue.text: Trainees one after another, we hear, succeeded

indicators.note: we hear tells us a phrase is to be taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: in turn means one after another, in sequence
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in family trees

explanation.surface: Trainees come forward in sequence, and it worked.
explanation.definitionFit: Interns are trainees or junior staff gaining work experience.

clue.text: Like some quote Kate recalled

indicators.note: called back, so the concealed run is read in reverse order
some of the words means only part of their letters are taken, a run concealed inside them

explanation.surface: Some quotation from Kate, remembered.
explanation.walkthrough: Read QUOTE KATE backwards (ETAKETOUQ) and the answer sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To take to someone is an idiom for starting to like them; both are verbs.

clue.text: Stork, say, crossing north, to go astray

indicators.note: crossing means stretching across, so the bird word goes around the compass letter

parts.note: a stork is an example of a wader, a long-legged wading bird

explanation.surface: A stork heading north drifts off course.
explanation.definitionFit: To wander can mean to stray from the right path or route.

clue.text: Get dancing? Ay! In arrangement this facilitates?

definitions.text: Get dancing? Ay! In arrangement this facilitates?

indicators.note: the letters put into a new arrangement are reordered to spell something else

explanation.surface: An eager yes to going out dancing, which a matchmaking service arranges.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: getting couples out dancing is what such a service sets up.
explanation.definitionFit: A dating agency matches people for romantic outings, such as going dancing together.

clue.text: Girl in church originally learnt Old English

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so only the first letter is used

explanation.surface: A girl at church first learnt Old English there.
explanation.definitionFit: Chloe is a girl's name, so it is an example of a girl.

clue.text: Numerical fact — something tried and trusted primarily

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so each word gives its first letter

explanation.surface: A reliable figure is something tested and trusted above all.
explanation.definitionFit: A stat, short for statistic, is a piece of numerical data.

clue.text: Fabulous girl in dream, I'm excited!

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: An excited exclamation about a wonderful girl seen in a dream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous' here means belonging to fable, not marvellous.
explanation.definitionFit: A mermaid is a legendary sea-creature, half woman, the stuff of fables and myth.

clue.text: Small area one's leased

parts.note: one gives I, and the 's stands for 'is', making I'S
let means rented out or leased

explanation.surface: A tiny plot of land that a person has rented out.
explanation.definitionFit: An islet is a very small island, a small area of land surrounded by water.

clue.text: Tyneside road — cosy place

parts.note: Tyneside, around Newcastle, is in the North East of England, abbreviated NE
ST, street, is a common abbreviation for a road

explanation.surface: A snug spot on a road in the Newcastle area.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyneside is the area around Newcastle upon Tyne in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A nest is used figuratively for any snug, comfortable retreat or home.

clue.text: What enhances appearance of Lorna, men think

indicators.note: of signals that the letters come out of the following words, sitting inside them

explanation.surface: Men's opinion of what makes Lorna look good.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornament is a decoration, something added to improve how a thing looks.
